text: Right where we left off: Sora at the end of the husk bridge, crossbow on Jaeha, and everyone behind her frozen.
She doesn't even turn her head. Everyone behind her stays very still, or the Operator gets a new hole.
On her wrist, the compass needle trembles between two pulses behind her.
Jaeha isn't watching the bolt. He's watching her wrist. She isn't watching the ones behind her. She's watching the needle.
She's the best shot in Seoul, Moon Ahin whispers. Jaeha knows. She told him so over a convenience-store coffee.
Nib creeps one step left. The needle snaps left, and without looking, Sora shoots the tip off his scarf, an inch from his neck.
Lyra draws. The needle snaps right, and Sora splits Lyra's arrow on the string, again without looking.
She reloads with one flick. The compass sees what she doesn't. Two pulses, two shots.
One minute thirty-one, and the rim narrows another notch.
The Director wants him alive, she smiles. He didn't say in how many pieces.
But Jaeha has it. She shoots where the needle points. So he'll move the needle.
Through LINK, his silent line to every summon, three orders. Nib, left again, fast. Borro, in front of Lyra. Lyra, wait for the thunder.
Borro flares back into field form in front of Lyra. A new, stronger pulse.
The needle swings right, then snaps back left.
Because Nib explodes off the ledge at her left side, knives drawn, the closest pulse she has.
Sora spins left after the needle.
In mid-leap, Jaeha drops Nib into rest form, which the compass can't see. Nib falls flat behind Number One.
With the left pulse gone, the needle swings all the way right, to the two bright pulses there.
Sora spins after it, loads a heavy bolt with a violet core, and fires where the needle points.
Straight into Borro's shield. It explodes in violet light, and Borro slides back into Lyra, who nocks an arrow behind him.
Jaeha PASSes the blow through his own body, from Borro to Lyra, losing thirty percent. Blood bursts from his nose, and Moon Ahin holds him up.
Moon Ahin flicks her baton once. Number One. Hold her.
Number One lets go of the stump with one hand and clamps it round Sora's ankle. She can't step aside.
Borrowed Thunder, part two. Lyra's arrow leaves the bow with the boom of Sora's own heavy bolt behind it.
It hits the compass, not Sora. Brass shatters, and the core needle spins away into the abyss.
Sora stares at her bare wrist, just a thin red line where the chain was.
Then she laughs, delighted. Director Baek is going to love him.
She twists free, flips off the bridge onto the ledge, and is gone through the side door, still laughing.
Lyra protests that she could have hit Sora's heart. Jaeha knows. Thank you for not.
Another husk falls. Fifty-eight seconds.
Moon Ahin half carries Jaeha the last few metres, cracks running under every step.
Borro scoops them both onto the ledge, and the white threads snap loose from Jaeha one by one.
Moon Ahin raises her baton. Come back to her, all of them. Twenty-eight husks climb up each other onto the ledge.
The rim is down to a slit a metre wide, sparks raining from the iris.
Borro jams his shield into the gap and heaves the steel plates apart with his back.
Borro holds doors. That's what he does. Go!
The crew squeeze through into the white, pushing and pulling each other.
Twenty-eight husks pour through two by two, faster than they've ever moved.
Borro's arms tremble. Twelve seconds.
Lyra dives through, then Nib. Moon Ahin stops in the gap and looks back.
Jaeha stumbles and nearly falls. Number Four!
She grabs his wrist and hauls him into the white. Borro lets go and dives after them as the iris slams shut.
Black. Gate rim sealed.
They tumble out onto the riverbank mud under the bridge, all of them in a heap. Behind them, the gate is gone behind a dark steel plate.
The crew lie on their backs under the orange lights. Uncle Pyo laughs without a sound. Woo and Ho hold each other.
Moon Ahin sits up, caked in mud, and counts her husks. Twenty-eight. And Number One.
But one figure lies face down in the mud. Operator, Nib begs. Everyone came back. He has to come back too.
One eye opens. Did he count everyone?
Nib nods fast. Everyone. Even the husks.
Torch beams run at them from the containers, and police lights come flashing down the riverside road.
Moon Ahin stands between the guards and the team. She is Moon Ahin, and anyone who touches these people gets their arms broken by her husks.
The guards skid to a stop.
Jaeha rolls over and fumbles out his phone. He should tell Seoa he's coming home.
Seoa has been texting. Are you alive? Answer me. All he manages is one letter: o.
His thumb jerks over the screen. It can't land on a key.
The phone slips out of his hands into the mud.
He holds his hands up against the bridge lights. They shake so hard they blur.
For the first time all night, Jaeha is confused. Stop shaking. Why won't they stop?
Beside his head, the phone buzzes. Seoa: o? What is o? Jaeha?
